name: context-menu
behavior: APG menu pattern invoked by context action (pointer contextmenu, Shift+F10, or the ContextMenu key on the focused target; the panel opens at the invocation point with focus moved to it; arrow keys rove focus; Home/End jump; typeahead; Esc closes and returns focus to the target; role=menu / role=menuitem)

parts.note: the target region, not a button: it carries no visible chrome and no aria-haspopup — it only owns the contextmenu/Shift+F10 handlers and must be focusable so keyboard invocation exists

anatomyNotes: Part-for-part identical to anatomy/dropdown-menu.json — dropdown-menu is normative for the shared parts. The whole difference is invocation and anchoring: a context menu has no visible trigger control and positions its panel at the pointer (or at the focused target's box for keyboard invocation) instead of anchoring to a trigger's edge. Salt has no context menu; its Menu covers the dropdown case only, so the behavior here is adopted straight from APG (states.md §Behavior contract). Destructive items are emphasis:danger at item level, as in dropdown-menu.
